previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and medically refractory hypoglycemia (nesidioblastosis) was admitted to the surgery service for gastrostomy tube placement to help stabilize blood sugars and assess response to gastric feeding. She underwent a laparoscopic procedure converted to open gastrostomy tube placement with intraoperative colotomy repair, recovered with pain control transitioned from hydromorphone PCA to oral oxycodone, and was monitored for intermittent tachycardia without instability. Her postoperative course was complicated by paralytic ileus with abdominal distention and delayed contrast transit on abdominal radiographs without free air; bowel function returned by postoperative day 4, after which continuous high-protein/moderate-carbohydrate tube feeds were initiated and advanced to goal with stable glucose levels. She remained afebrile without infectious complications, ambulated independently, tolerated bariatric stage 5 diet plus continuous enteral nutrition, received G-tube care and glucose-monitoring education, and was discharged home with services on continuous tube feeds and follow-up arranged.

You underwent reopening and debridement of your abdominal wound

you.
